Favicon: the favicon candidate chooser answers no candidate when the engine's file-URL rule refuses that candidate for the page's base URL, so no probe starts and no cached file: icon is served to a remote page; a file: page's favicon still loads.

body: Favicon gate: the favicon candidate chooser answers none for a candidate (the page's link rel=icon href, else /favicon.ico joined to its base URL) that the engine's document_may_load refuses for that base URL, so the probe is never started; a file: document's favicon candidate is still chosen and loads.

The favicon cache is keyed by candidate and shared across tabs and stores positive results only: gating at the candidate chooser, before the cache is reached, keeps a file: icon a file: page cached from being served to a remote page naming the same URL.

Navigation gate: the browser navigation provider, built once per document by the document config builder, takes that document's URL there and refuses, loading nothing, a navigation document_may_load(document URL, target) refuses; a document with no URL (the error page) counts as no file: document. The navigating document is not read from the navigation options' source document id nor from the tab's current history entry.

The navigation gate binds only document-started navigations that reach navigate_to (link clicks, keyboard-activated links and submits, form submissions of the top document); the user's own top-level loads (URL bar, history, home, new-tab and history pages, initial URL) keep going out as top-level requests with no initiator.

The engine's file-URL rule (file URLs only for file documents, refused FileForbidden before any disk read) and the public blitz-traits document_may_load are used as they stand, neither widened nor narrowed; the request initiator meaning and the engine's sub-resource initiator stamping are not changed and no engine crate is edited.
A refused favicon or navigation is simply not started: a filter and an early return, with no new error type, cause, log line, tracing call, span, env read, listener or dependency.

Behave like a browser and cite the spec: the silent refusal follows Chromium and Firefox, and the Fetch standard's scheme-fetch (which leaves file: to the implementation) is cited at the implementation.

Favicon check: a unit test of the pure favicon candidate chooser in the favicon component's existing test module, covering a remote page naming a file: candidate (none) and a file: page's file: candidate (kept); no network provider, temp file or TMPDIR read.

Navigation check: a new unit-test module at the end of the navigation provider's file calls navigate_to on a History store built inside a VirtualDom, the way the tab store lens test builds one, covering a remote document navigating to a file: URL (nothing loads) and a file: document doing so (it loads).
Both new checks run in the workspace test leg with no disk read, so the three CI operating systems read them alike.
Every new check carries a control: the mutation or hand edit that turns it red, and the reading that it did.

The capability statement's only change is dropping the two provisional clauses (the fixture-state absence, and exploration on no carrier and following no navigation); the browser's two closed paths are not added to it and its Loading pages limit, which speaks of the engine, is unchanged.

every change passes the format, clippy and rustdoc-warnings gates

It also added `+ decision/one-stamping-request-constructor`, a blitz-dom clippy rule that allows only the stamping constructor. This chunk calls the public `document_may_load` as it stands. body: The rule that a file: URL loads only for a file document now binds the app's own favicon candidate choice and the app's own top-document navigations: each is checked with document_may_load(loading document URL, target) before anything starts.

The engine's sub-resource rule and its FileForbidden refusal are used as they stand, neither widened nor narrowed; the app reads the public blitz_traits::net::document_may_load and no engine crate changes.

Favicon candidate choice: favicon_candidate answers none for a candidate the rule refuses for the page's base URL, so no fetch is started and a file: icon a file page cached is never served to a remote page naming the same URL; a file document's favicon still loads.
The favicon fetch itself goes out through blitz-net's Request::get with no initiator, read as a top-level load; the chunk gates before that fetch rather than relying on the fetch to refuse.

In-document navigation from a non-file document to a file: URL is refused silently and loads nothing; the navigating document's URL is taken where its navigation provider is built, not from the tab's current history entry, so a remote page still shown while a typed file page loads cannot reach a file: URL.
A document with no URL, the browser's error page, counts as no file document for the navigation rule; error pages already skip history and favicon probing.

Link clicks, keyboard-activated links and submits, and form submissions of the top document all reach navigate_to; the refusal sits ahead of the existing external-target and form-submission scheme and method handling, which stays as it is.
The user's own top-level loads — the URL bar, history, home, the new-tab and history pages, the initial URL — still load whatever they name, file: included.

No carrier, verb, argument, cause, session error, exit, log field, span, env read, listener or dependency is added: a refused favicon or navigation is a filter or an early return, reaching no error path and no tracing call.

Each new check carries a control, the mutation or hand edit that turns it red and the reading that it did; the favicon gate is unit-tested as the pure favicon_candidate, the navigation gate by calling navigate_to on a History store built inside a VirtualDom, with no disk read, temp file or TMPDIR read, so the three CI OSes read them alike in the workspace test leg.

The capability statement loses only its two provisional clauses; the browser's two closed paths are not added to it, since the browser app is upstream's and its loading-pages limit speaks of the engine's rule, which this chunk does not move.

Snapshot, accessibility, stable element id, masked control values, select list and other control-state readings: the chunk changes no engine reader and no carrier.
Recorded checks, kept check files, cold-agent runs, coverage floors and the coverage answer: no recording, replay or coverage path is touched.

Script fetcher scheme limits, JS fetch method limits and the same-origin and CORS absences: same-origin, CORS and other schemes such as data: and about: are out of scope, and script fetches are not touched.

Iframe navigation routing, iframe and import nesting limits and stale iframe responses: an iframe's navigation already goes through the engine's own provider and stamping constructor, out of this chunk's scope.
CI tokens, CI secrets, signing material, publish and release jobs and the WPT workflows: no CI job, workflow or secret is added or changed.
Engine parse, style, layout and paint rules (CSS, HTML parsing, presentational hints, transforms, serialization): the chunk edits no engine crate.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** — (amd-bn47lomj, `~ decision/file-urls-only-for-file-documents` rule) widened the rule from script loads alone to every engine sub-resource load through blitz-net: a non-`file:` document reads no local file. This chunk closes the two app-side paths, the favicon probe and navigation, that this widening left open. The rule's wording names engine and script loads only, so the chunk's two checks either extend this row or stand beside it.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** — (amd-gso2bo7y, `~ decision/file-urls-only-for-file-documents` guard) added `local_files_for_local_documents` to the row's guard list beside the two script-load checks. It sets the precedent: a check that holds a new half of the `file:` rule joins the row's guard. The favicon and navigation checks are candidates for the same list.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** — (amd-qi7vgvwx, `+ decision/real-provider-inside-stand-in`) the previous chunk's witness put blitz-net's real provider behind a hand-written stand-in on its own runtime. This chunk's scope departs from that on purpose: no `StdNetProvider`, temp file or `TMPDIR` read. The favicon gate is unit-tested on the pure `favicon_candidate`, and the navigation gate is reached through `navigate_to` on an in-VirtualDom `History`. The plan should state that departure.

**2026-11-13-local-files-for-local-documents** — (amd-lde2vbr3, `+ decision/blitz-dom-requests-through-stamping-constructor`) a crate-level clippy config makes blitz-dom build every request through one stamping constructor, which sets the initiator. `apps/browser` has no such guard: its `Request::get` without an initiator is the gap the favicon path exposes. The plan should not assume that clippy guard reaches the app.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (amd-6q2sqo5s) Script ↔ DOM gained the `file:` URL narrowing (`document_may_load`). Its tests are `remote_document_cannot_load_file_urls` and `file_document_can_load_sibling_file_urls`, and the `file:` URLs are read on the macOS and Windows CI legs beside linux's. These are the origin of the row's guards. A test that reads files would need to hold on all three OSes; this chunk's checks avoid disk entirely.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (amd-cp6hvbjs) the two `file:`-load script tests write sibling files under `std::env::temp_dir()` through a test-only `TMPDIR` read (`temp_dir_with_files`), counted as an occupied resource. This is the precedent this chunk's scope steers away from; adding a disk-touching check would add a further test-only `TMPDIR` site.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (amd-rf4xxwvm) recorded `apps/browser/src/tab.rs`'s test module, with one `#[test]`, `tab_lens_survives_webview_props_replacement`. It is the browser's sixth tested file, beside about_pages, browser_history, favicon, url_suggestions and persistence, and runs in the workspace `test` leg. This chunk extends `favicon.rs`'s existing test module and adds a new test module to `history.rs`, built on tab.rs's in-VirtualDom pattern. The §1 and §4 apps/browser inventories (the list of tested files and their counts) move with it.

**2026-10-27-upstream-sync-engine-debts** — (amd-simkhsnt) the workspace tally's +8 passed was attributed by name, `apps/browser/src/tab.rs` 1 among them. This is the precedent that browser unit tests land in an existing result line of the workspace `test` leg, not in a new one, so the chunk's re-count moves passed and not result lines.

**2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces** — (amd-u6pbkyf3) recorded that blitz-net's `file:` read through `Url::to_file_path` has no test named for it. The navigation and favicon gates refuse before that read, so they still do not test it, and the absence stands.

**2026-11-01-upstream-sync-ui-graph** — (amd-6o3k2s3y) blitz-net gained 3 unit tests, two of them binding a loopback `TcpListener`. It kept the record that the `file:` read has no test named for it. The chunk reads `blitz_traits::net::document_may_load` as it stands and adds no blitz-net test.

**2026-11-14-auto-exploration** — (amd-knbkpfwu, `~ decision/mutation-controlled-tests` rule) the controlled-tests rule now adds that a control removing a bound loosens it to twice the budget. The scope requires every new check to carry a control (inputs#I1). For example, a mutation that drops the `document_may_load` filter in `favicon_candidate`, or the early return in `navigate_to`, should turn the new tests red, and the restored tree should read green.

**2026-10-16-fast-failing-mutants** — (amd-le75xddb) set the mutation tier's recipe: cargo-mutants with `--test-tool nextest` under the `mutants` profile and `--baseline=skip`, each unit's test command read green first, on the dev host only and never in CI. This is the origin of the picked rows `decision/mutation-baseline-read-per-unit`, `decision/mutation-testing-dev-host-only`, `decision/mutation-baseline-skipped`, `decision/mutation-runs-on-dev-host-only` and `decision/mutation-runs-under-nextest-profile`. Any mutation control run on the browser app follows this recipe.

**2026-11-14-start-in-a-state** — (amd-lfmouigx, `~ decision/inline-cfg-test-modules` except) dropped the stated count of out-of-line `#[path]` test modules from the exception. The new `history.rs` test module is planned inline at the file's end, inside this row's rule, so no exception is needed.

It also records a trap: a sed or grep address ending at a function's name also selects items whose names start with it, and a control built on the same address cannot catch that. This matters for controls on `favicon_candidate` and `navigate_to`.

**2026-10-16-file-splits** — (amd-dvdqody5) moved test modules out of line with `#[cfg(test)]` and `#[path]` at their parent, test paths unchanged. This is the precedent the `decision/unit-tests-in-source-file` row states for a module moved out of line. It applies only if a browser test module grows out of its source file.

**2026-10-07-driver-command-spans** — (amd-s53lzeiq) the same check read green per package and red in the workspace leg. This is the origin of `decision/per-package-green-not-workspace-green`. The chunk's checks run in the workspace `test` leg, so a green `cargo test -p` on the browser app is not that leg's green.

**2026-10-10-upstream-sync-agent-surfaces** — (amd-cqdq6a7d) found that the workspace and per-package builds resolve different engine features (`writing-mode`, `tracing`). This sharpened the per-package-green rule: the two builds can compile different code under the same test.

**2026-10-05-fork-ci-reached** — (amd-dhibncze) made the workspace tests the fast `test` leg (`cargo test --workspace --locked`), with the matrix testing windows and macos and only building ios and android. This is the origin of `decision/workspace-tests-in-fast-ci-leg` and `decision/native-platform-ci-matrix`. The browser checks run where the scope says: linux in the `test` leg, windows and macos in the matrix. With no disk read, all three OSes should read them alike.

**2026-11-07-mounteddata-buffered-render** — (amd-jy34nxjf) set the rule for re-reading per-OS tallies: in a GitHub Actions job log, the `Running …` lines and the `test result:` lines do not interleave in order, so a tally move is attributed by grepping the test's own name, beside the ANSI strip. This applies when the chunk re-counts its browser unit tests on CI.

**2026-10-25-capability-statement** — (amd-472linzq) added `test_capability_statement.py` (`CapabilityStatementTest`). It pins the verb and cause names and the counts in `docs/capabilities.md`, plus the README's MCP tool count, and adds the claims-to-checks map in which only names and counts are pinned. This is the origin of the capability-statement rows. The chunk edits `docs/capabilities.md` only to drop the CARRY's two «provisional» clauses. That edit must leave the pinned names and counts untouched so the ci-scripts leg stays green.

**2026-11-08-handler-coverage** — (amd-hf3zl3jw) the capability statement's claim map gained three stated limits, each with its owner, under `decision/capability-claims-name-their-checks`. This is the precedent for how a limit's wording in `docs/capabilities.md` changes when its status moves. The chunk's dropped «provisional» clauses are such a move, and the scope decides that the browser's closed paths are not added as claims.

**2026-10-31-select-popup** — (amd-krjdo5z6) the `docs/capabilities.md` select limits went from two bullets to four, each read by named checks. This is a precedent for editing the capabilities doc by hand under the claims-to-checks map. The map's names and counts are a hand edit when a check is renamed or moved.

**2026-11-14-auto-exploration** — (amd-3ieo66hz, `+ contract/session-recording/exploration-checks`) added the exploration-checks contract row, a picked row. Exploration follows no navigation (the founder's F2 A), and that is one of the `docs/capabilities.md` clauses at lines 346–347 whose «provisional» this chunk's CARRY drops. The row itself is unchanged by this chunk.

The reference browser app (apps/browser, the blitz binary) closes the two paths by which a remote page still makes the browser read a local file.
The favicon path: a favicon candidate a non-file: document names under file: is never chosen, so it is never probed nor served from the shared favicon cache; a file: document's favicon still loads.
The navigation path: a link click or form submission a non-file: document starts to a file: URL loads nothing, silently; one a file: document starts still loads, and the user's own top-level loads are unchanged.
Both gates read the engine's existing document_may_load rule as it stands; no engine crate is edited.
It also drops two stale provisional clauses from the capability statement, where the founder has ruled.

body_fields.what: the browser app's favicon component — choosing a page's favicon candidate and probing it, with its inline unit test module — edits: the function favicon_candidate, its existing test module

the browser app's navigation provider over the tab's history store, through which every top-document link click and form submission navigates — edits: BrowserNavProvider and its navigate_to, a new test module at the end of the file

the browser app's document loader, which builds each document's config and its navigation provider once per document, holding that document's base URL — edits: the function make_doc_config, the one construction site of BrowserNavProvider

escher's capability statement, the document of what escher can and cannot do, pinned to the driver schema — edits: the provisional clause on the fixture-state absence and the provisional clause on exploration on no carrier and following no navigation

body: The favicon gate: favicon_candidate answers no candidate when document_may_load with the page's base URL refuses that candidate, so a non-file: page naming a file: icon (by link href or by /favicon.ico joined to a file: base) starts no probe; a file: page's file: favicon is still chosen and loads.

The shared favicon cache, keyed by candidate and shared across tabs: because the gate sits before the cache is reached, a file: icon a file: page cached is never served to a remote page naming the same URL.

The navigation gate: BrowserNavProvider takes its document's URL when make_doc_config builds it, and navigate_to returns early, loading nothing, for a navigation document_may_load(document URL, target) refuses; a document with no URL (the error page) counts as no file: document; a file: document's navigation to a file: URL still loads.

The navigating document is the provider's own document, never the tab's current history entry: a remote page still displayed while a file: page the user typed loads must not reach a file: URL. The user's own top-level loads (URL bar, history, home, the new-tab and history pages, the initial URL) do not pass through the gate.

Indirect, through the engine's net traits: the engine rule that file: URLs are loadable only from a file: document (document_may_load, FileForbidden) is used as it stands, neither widened nor narrowed; the app reads the public function and adds no rule of its own.

A refusal is silent: no carrier, verb, argument, refusal cause, session error, exit code, log field, span, tracing call, env read, listener or dependency is added; a refused favicon or navigation is a filter and an early return, reaching no error path and no log line.
Every new check carries a control: the mutation or hand edit that turns it red (dropping the favicon filter, dropping the navigate_to early return) and the reading that it did.

The favicon gate is proved as a pure unit test of favicon_candidate inside favicon.rs's existing inline test module: remote base with a file: href and a file: favicon fallback refused, file: base with a file: candidate kept, remote candidates kept.

The navigation gate is proved in a new inline test module at the end of history.rs, calling BrowserNavProvider::navigate_to on a History store built inside a VirtualDom the way the tab lens test builds one, and reading that the history gained no entry for a refused file: target and gained one for an allowed target.
The new tests read no disk and need no real network provider, temp file or TMPDIR: they run in the workspace test leg and read alike on the three CI OSes.

The capability statement edit only drops the two provisional clauses; the statement stays pinned to the driver schema, its claim section names and counts unchanged, and the browser's two closed paths are not added to it.
No capability is claimed by this chunk: no 0.3.0 capability names this entry.

body_fields.convention: every new test is controlled red-before-green — the mutation or hand edit that turns it red, and the reading that it did
unit tests sit in an inline test module of their own source file, not in a new test target
a regression test documents and is named for the bug it pins
test data is stated in code — fixture URLs and documents written in the test, nothing seeded or read from disk
test failures print no argument value, and a table-driven test asserts its row count
stand-ins are hand-written, with no mocking library
no sleep or wall-clock read in a check
workspace tests run in the fast CI leg across the native platform matrix

The seven_guis headless stand, its boot functions, stand log and stand-check rules (both layout modes, bundled font, three-round repeat): the stand and the seven_guis app are untouched.

WPT conformance runner, its CLI, outputs, status set and suites: no engine conformance behaviour moves.
Harness construction, core, settle, input, inspection, contrast and screenshot contracts: the new tests drive no escher harness and take no screenshot.
Lint defects, driver refusal causes, snapshot nodes and handler coverage limits: no lint, cause or coverage reading is added or changed.
Recorded and committed checks, their freshness and replay: no check is recorded.
Pixel and font tests, buffered render, select painting and scrollbar fade: nothing painted changes.
CI workflow plumbing — pinned actions, package installs, cache, secrets, artifacts, coverage-floor and apt-install script exit codes: no CI job or script is added or edited.
